A drug that works re-enters phase 1 as a combination partner,
so its own phase sequence stops being a sequence. The ordering
is only legible while a compound is young — and those keys
have the fewest trials and the least follow-up, which is the
opposite of where the statistical power is.
the join works; the meaning does not
Normalised intervention names give 16,676 keys spanning two or more phases across 162,173
trials, and spot-checked raw they collapse correctly. But the largest are cyclophosphamide,
cisplatin and carboplatin — backbone agents appearing in other drugs' trials at every phase
for fifty years. This register can compare phases in aggregate; it cannot follow one product
ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, fetched 2026-09-22; intervention names from a third walk. Keys are DRUG and BIOLOGICAL intervention names, lowercased with
dose and formulation tokens stripped and placebo-like terms dropped — a deliberately shallow rule, because a deeper one starts merging distinct
molecules. Drawn: the 7,553 keys with at least five trials spanning at least two phases. A trial listing several drugs contributes to each, so a phase
3 trial of one drug on a standard backbone counts for both.
